title: Discrete random variables
overview: Build probability distributions, calculate expectation and variance, and apply the binomial distribution. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Construct discrete probability distributions and find unknown constants.
Use and recognise binomial and geometric models.
Find exact, cumulative and complementary probabilities.

definitions.definition: A variable taking separate countable numerical values.
A table or rule assigning a probability to each possible value.
The number of successes in n independent fixed-probability trials.
The trial number of the first success in independent trials with probability p.

sections.title: Distribution tables
content: List every possible x and P(X=x), require each probability ≥0 and use ΣP(X=x)=1 to find constants. Then E(X)=ΣxP(X=x), E(X²)=Σx²P(X=x), and Var(X)=E(X²)−[E(X)]².
bullets: Probabilities, not x-values, must sum to 1.

sections.title: Binomial model
content: X~B(n,p) requires a fixed number n, two outcomes per trial, constant success probability p and independent trials. Use P(X=r)=ⁿCᵣpʳ(1−p)ⁿ⁻ʳ, with mean np and variance np(1−p).
bullets: Translate 'at most', 'fewer than' and 'at least' carefully.
Use complements for long upper tails.

sections.title: Geometric model
content: For X~Geo(p), where X is the trial of first success, P(X=r)=p(1−p)ʳ⁻¹ and E(X)=1/p. The memoryless idea means after failures the chance of success on the next trial remains p.
bullets: The support begins at r=1, not 0.
Do not use a fixed n in a geometric model.

sections.title: Using a calculator
content: A calculator may evaluate cumulative probabilities, but the model, parameters and inequality conversion must be shown. For P(X>r), use 1−P(X≤r); for P(a≤X≤b), subtract cumulative values.
bullets: Check whether calculator cumulative commands include the endpoint.
State the distribution before the probability statement.

examTips: Write X~B(n,p) or X~Geo(p) before calculating.
Translate the words into an exact integer inequality before pressing the calculator.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using binomial when the success probability changes.

quickRecall.question: What four conditions support a binomial model?
quickRecall.answer: Fixed n, two outcomes, independent trials and constant success probability p.

quickRecall.question: What does a geometric variable count?
quickRecall.answer: The trial number on which the first success occurs.
